Also, the summary in the lede should probably briefly mention Odysseus's wanderings.

I cannot express how much I loathe sidebar navboxes. They take up tons of space that could be used for text and useful illustrations and, in my opinion, they don't add anything constructive. If a link isn't in the article somewhere or even in the "see also" at the bottom, it probably isn't relevant. If you absolutely need to have one, three is way too many. At the very least, limit it to just one. (I would go with the "Trojan War" one myself, since it's the most specific.)

listing some themes discussed in the body that really are crucial to the poem

A bit of false framing here. Women probably had more influence in ancient Greece than they have traditionally been given credit for. What's really significant is that the women and slaves have more prominent roles in the poem than in other works of ancient literature (such as the *Iliad*).

There is no reason why these deserve to be mentioned in the lede, especially since neither is mentioned in the body. Non-linear structure is practically ubiquitous throughout ancient Greek literature, so the *Odyssey* is hardly unique in this regard. An unreliable narrator is most applicable only significant insofar as the story of Odyssey's wanderings is concerned and this isn't discussed in the body at all.
